answer: Timed quartz drift attestation. Each agent must return a hardware-timestamped quartz clock drift reading over a random interval; a single operator can simulate identities but cannot physically hold thousands of independently drifting oscillators in sync. A ripple in drift error across claimed devices exposes cloned hardware, forcing attackers to buy and maintain real clocks per identity. Every false voyage into the network costs full physical hardware plus continuous power, making mass forgery economically impossible at scale.
